title: For IPv4 subnets whose DNS nameserver order range is greater than the avera
question: For IPv4 subnets whose DNS nameserver order range is greater than the average order range across all IPv4 subnets, return each subnet name along with its DNS nameserver order range, order variance, coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the order values, and the deviation of that coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.

prediction.sql:
WITH subnet_measures AS (
  SELECT
    s.id AS subnet_id,
    s.name AS subnet_name,
    MAX(d.`order`) - MIN(d.`order`) AS order_range,
    VARIANCE(d.`order`) AS order_variance,
    STDDEV(d.`order`) / NULLIF(AVG(d.`order`), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation
  FROM `subnets` AS s
  JOIN `dnsnameservers` AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id
  WHERE s.ip_version = 4
  GROUP BY s.id, s.name
),
avg_measures AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(order_range) AS average_order_range,
    AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS average_coefficient_of_variation
  FROM subnet_measures
)
SELECT
  sm.subnet_name,
  sm.order_range,
  sm.order_variance,
  sm.coefficient_of_variation,
  sm.coefficient_of_variation - am.average_coefficient_of_variation AS deviation_from_avg_coefficient_of_variation
FROM subnet_measures AS sm
CROSS JOIN avg_measures AS am
WHERE sm.order_range > am.average_order_range

       VARIANCE(d.`order`) AS order_variance,
       STDDEV(d.`order`) / AVG(d.`order`) AS cv,
       (STDDEV(d.`order`) / AVG(d.`order`)) - (SELECT AVG(sub_cv.cv) FROM (
           SELECT STDDEV(d2.`order`) / AVG(d2.`order`) AS cv

JOIN dnsnameservers d ON d.subnet_id = s.id

GROUP BY s.id, s.name

        JOIN dnsnameservers d3 ON d3.subnet_id = s3.id
        WHERE s3.ip_version = 4
